phone_messages_react_lens.summary:
ZOOM (symptom 1): iOS Safari zooms in when a text field with a font size under 16px gets focus, and it stays zoomed after the field loses focus. The phone Messages screen has two such fields. The composer textarea is 14.5px (MessagesMobile.tsx:1318). The New-message search field is 15px (2791) and is focused in code 60 ms after that screen opens (2620-2625). The viewport export sets only width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover (layout.tsx:27-32). Once the page is off its initial scale, WebKit turns double-tap zoom back on (WebKit blog), and nothing in src sets touch-action: manipulation (grep found nothing). So after the first auto-zoom, double taps zoom as well. Commit 5b62ff5 did not cause the zoom. The textarea and the search autofocus date from 2026-05-14 (blame c2206cdf and bb1a27f5), and `git log -S maximumScale` on layout.tsx returns nothing, so the viewport never had it.

UNINTENDED ACTIONS (symptom 2):
- Cause 1, the long-press reaction picker. It arms on every pointerdown, fires at 360 ms, and is cancelled only by 10 px of movement or a pointer end. It does not notice scrolling or a touch that stops a momentum scroll. 5b62ff5 put the same handlers on photos, videos (including the native controls), shared-post cards and notice tiles, so the area that can open it grew a lot. The picker opens right above the bubble, and the next tap there posts a reaction.
- Cause 2, the conversation's swipe-to-close. The conversation is a vaul drawer set to close by swiping right. vaul treats any horizontal drift during a scroll as a drag. It then runs its release logic even after iOS cancels the pointer to scroll, and it closes when the finger moved faster than 0.4 px per ms.
- The 5b62ff5 onClickCapture guard is sound. longPressFired can stay true after a release that produces no click, but the next pointerdown resets it (3006). So it cannot swallow a later tap; the only exception is a click with no pointerdown before it, such as a VoiceOver activation.

Minimal fixes:
- Set both fields to 16px.
- Add touch-action: manipulation, including on the message-list scroller.
- Long-press: raise the timer to about 500 ms, cancel it on scroll, and do not arm it on the video.
- Pass handleOnly to the conversation's Drawer.Root.
- maximum-scale=1 is not needed once the fields are 16px.

findings.title: Composer textarea (14.5px) and New-message search (15px, auto-focused on open) trigger iOS focus auto-zoom
findings.symptom: Page zooms in when a thread's message box is tapped, or immediately when 'New message' opens; zoom persists after blur and across client-side navigation, so the next visit to Messages is still zoomed ('sometimes when I open messages it zooms in').
findings.root_cause: iOS Safari auto-zooms the visual viewport when a text input/textarea whose computed font-size is under 16px receives focus, unless the viewport caps scale. The inline styles set 14.5px (textarea) and 15px (search); inline beats Tailwind preflight's `font: inherit`, and no stylesheet overrides with !important, so computed size = the inline value. The viewport has no maximum-scale. Opening a thread does NOT focus the textarea (vaul prevents open autofocus), so the zoom happens on the first tap into the composer; the compose search is focused programmatically 60 ms after mount, so that screen zooms as it opens.
findings.evidence: src/components/mobile/MessagesMobile.tsx:1292-1323 <textarea> fontSize 14.5 at :1318 (blame c2206cdf, 2026-05-14); :932 send() finally re-focuses it. :2620-2625 ComposeOverlay `setTimeout(() => inputRef.current?.focus(), 60)` (blame bb1a27f5, 2026-05-14); :2775-2795 search <input> fontSize 15 at :2791. Group rename input :2153-2171 is 17px (:2166) so it does not zoom. src/app/layout.tsx:27-32 viewport = {width:'device-width', initialScale:1, viewportFit:'cover'}, no maximumScale/interactiveWidget; `git log -S maximumScale -- src/app/layout.tsx` returns nothing (never had it). node_modules/vaul/dist/index.mjs:1476-1481 Content prevents onOpenAutoFocus unless autoFocus (default false, :879), and node_modules/@radix-ui/react-dialog/dist/index.mjs:146-149 onCloseAutoFocus preventDefault + focuses the (absent) trigger — so neither opening nor closing a sheet focuses the textarea. vaul's iOS scroll-lock also focuses inputs itself on touchend (vaul index.mjs:216-230, active per :939-941), which still opens the keyboard and zooms. ConversationView is shared with CampusMobile (CampusMobile.tsx:18, :493), so Campus chat has the same zoom. Platform rule: CSS-Tricks '16px or Larger Text Prevents iOS Form Zoom' (https://css-tricks.com/16px-or-larger-text-prevents-ios-form-zoom/).
findings.fix: MessagesMobile.tsx:1318 fontSize 14.5 → 16 (trim padding at :1309 from '10px 14px' to about '9px 14px' to keep the 38px min height). :2791 fontSize 15 → 16. Optionally drop the 60 ms programmatic focus at :2620-2625 so New message doesn't raise the keyboard until the user taps. maximum-scale=1 is NOT needed once inputs are ≥16px. On iOS it only suppresses this auto-zoom, since pinch has ignored it since iOS 10. On Android it blocks pinch-zoom, which fails WCAG 1.4.4.
findings.risk: Low. Composer text looks slightly larger. Desktop messages.html inputs are 13px (public/html/messages.html:77, 85, 192) but only render at ≥900px.

findings.title: Long-press reaction picker arms on every touch (360 ms / 10 px, no scroll awareness); 5b62ff5 spread it to photos, videos, post cards and tiles
findings.symptom: Resting a finger on a message, stopping a flick, or dragging slowly makes the emoji picker pop up. The next tap near that bubble lands on an emoji and sends a reaction the user never chose. Holding a video's native controls opens the picker.
findings.root_cause: startLongPress runs on pointerdown and fires setPickerOpen after 360 ms, shorter than iOS's native ~500 ms long-press. The only cancels are movement over 10 px (dx²+dy² > 100), pointerup, pointercancel and pointerleave. Nothing cancels on list scroll or momentum, nothing checks isPrimary, and navigator.vibrate is a no-op on iOS Safari, so the popup comes silently. Any touch that stays within 10 px for 0.36 s fires it: a finger parked while reading, a touch that catches a momentum scroll, or a slow drag under about 28 px/s. The picker is placed directly above the bubble. Its outside-dismiss runs only on pointerdown outside it, so a tap that lands on it hits an emoji button, which POSTs the reaction at once. 5b62ff5 widened this. The handlers were on the text bubble only (pre-S57 diff); they now also cover notice tiles, the photo wrapper (up to 260×320), the video wrapper around <video controls>, and the shared-post Link card (260 wide, 150 px poster). The S57 onClickCapture guard is correct. It swallows only the click right after a fired long-press. longPressFired stays true after a release with no click, since clearLongPress does not reset it, but the next pointerdown on that bubble resets it (:3006). The spread targets are siblings, not nested (:3484-3497), and the picker is not inside them, so emoji and chip clicks are never swallowed. pointerleave and pointercancel both clear the timer. vaul's setPointerCapture on every press (vaul :968) delays pointerleave, but pointerup and pointercancel still clear it.
findings.evidence: MessagesMobile.tsx:2998-3004 clearLongPress (does not touch longPressFired); :3005-3020 timer 360 ms, :3011-3017 navigator.vibrate; :3023-3028 cancel only at >10 px (:3027); :3034-3053 pressHandlers incl. onClickCapture :3047-3052 (all added by 5b62ff5 per blame). Spread sites: :3122 noticeTile, :3146 textBubble, :3182 video wrapper (<video controls> :3185), :3206 photo wrapper, :3251 post Link card. The pre-5b62ff5 diff shows the handlers only on the text bubble. ReactionPicker placement :3616-3618 (bottom: calc(100% + 6px)); dismiss on document pointerdown :3589-3604; emoji onClick → onPick :3641-3647 → toggleReaction :3557-3560 → POST/DELETE :936-975. Long-press logic dates from 52343e8 / ef2eb45 (2026-05-14).
findings.fix:
In MessageBubble:
(1) Raise the 360 at :3019 to about 500.
(2) Arm only for `e.isPrimary` touch/mouse presses (:3035).
(3) Cancel on scroll. For example, ConversationView's onScroll (:1183-1188) stamps a `lastScrollAtRef`, and the timer callback returns early if a scroll happened within about 150 ms. The minimal variant is to also call clearLongPress on the scroller's scroll event while pressed.
(4) Drop {...pressHandlers} from the video wrapper at :3182 so native controls never arm it. Keep it on the text, photo and card.
(5) Ignore emoji clicks for about 250 ms after the picker opens, or open the picker on the release after a hold.
findings.risk: Low to medium. The long-press becomes slightly slower, and the gesture needs a device test. Removing it from videos means reacting to a video needs a caption bubble or a different affordance.

findings.title: Once zoomed, double-tap zoom is live and nothing sets touch-action: manipulation
findings.symptom: After the first auto-zoom, quick double taps (tapping send twice, double-tapping a bubble or the list) zoom in or out again. The screen feels hypersensitive and hard to un-zoom.
findings.root_cause: WebKit gives width=device-width pages fast single taps (no double-tap zoom) only at initial scale. After the focus auto-zoom the page is off initial scale, so double-tap zoom returns. No element on this screen sets touch-action: manipulation, which disables double-tap zoom at every scale. vaul's injected `[data-vaul-drawer]{touch-action:none}` covers the drawer's header and composer, which sit outside the message-list scroller. So on those strips pinch gestures are likely ignored, and the user can only pinch back out from the message list (plausible, not device-verified).
findings.evidence: layout.tsx:27-32 (no scale cap, which is the right choice). `grep -rn 'touch-action: manipulation|touchAction: "manipulation"' src` returned nothing. globals.css has no touch-action rule; its only tap rule is -webkit-tap-highlight at :2605. Tailwind v4 preflight already sets -webkit-text-size-adjust:100% (node_modules/tailwindcss/preflight.css:31) and tap-highlight transparent (:45), so text inflation and the tap flash are ruled out. vaul CSS: node_modules/vaul/dist/index.mjs:62 `[data-vaul-drawer]{touch-action:none;...}`. The WebKit blog (https://webkit.org/blog/5610/more-responsive-tapping-on-ios/) says device-width fast tapping applies only at initial scale, and that touch-action: manipulation limits a clickable element's touches to panning and pinch zoom.
findings.fix: Add `touchAction: "manipulation"` inline on the ConversationView message-list scroller (MessagesMobile.tsx:1189-1194) and on MessagesMobile's <main> (:359-366). Alternatively add `html, body { touch-action: manipulation; }` in globals.css and still set it on the scroller, because WebKit likely resets touch-action at a scroll container (unverified). This keeps pan and pinch and removes double-tap zoom. Fixing the first finding removes the zoom that turns double-tap back on.
findings.risk: Low. Pinch-zoom still works. Children that set touch-action: none or pan-y (maps, cropper) still intersect correctly.

findings.title: Conversation drawer (vaul, direction=right) turns diagonal scroll drift into a drag and can close the thread mid-scroll
findings.symptom: While flicking through messages, the conversation jolts sideways or closes back to the thread list. If iOS still counts the gesture as a tap, the click lands on the thread row underneath and opens a different conversation.
findings.root_cause: ConversationView is a dismissible vaul Drawer with direction='right'. vaul puts pointer handlers on the whole Content. For horizontal drawers, shouldDrag() returns true unconditionally, skipping the scroll-parent, text-selection and 500 ms post-open checks that vertical drawers get. isDeltaInDirection locks drag mode on any leftward drift, or on rightward drift over 10 px, so onDrag starts translating the drawer. When iOS then takes over for native vertical scrolling it fires pointercancel and then pointerout. vaul has no pointercancel handler, but onPointerOut calls onRelease with the last pointermove. onRelease closes if velocity is over 0.4 px/ms at any distance, or if the drag is at least 25% of the width. vaul's close runs our onOpenChange(false) → onClose → setOpenThreadId(null), which unmounts the drawer at once (no exit animation), so a trailing synthetic click hits the list below.
findings.evidence: MessagesMobile.tsx:1006-1010 <Drawer.Root open direction="right" onOpenChange={(o)=>{ if(!o) onClose(); }}> (blame 61198317, 2026-05-14); :484-497 conditional mount; :492-495 onClose; :585-587 ThreadRow is a full-width onClick button. node_modules/vaul/dist/index.mjs:953-969 onPress on every pointerdown sets isDragging and setPointerCapture; :984-986 shouldDrag returns true for right/left; :1419-1441 isDeltaInDirection locks on reverse drift; :1505 swipeStartThreshold 10 for touch; :1522-1525 onPointerOut → handleOnPointerUp(lastKnownPointerEvent) → onRelease; :1258-1262 velocity > VELOCITY_THRESHOLD → closeDrawer; :446-447 VELOCITY_THRESHOLD 0.4, CLOSE_THRESHOLD 0.25; :1268 width × closeThreshold; :1173-1178 closeDrawer → setIsOpen(false) → our onOpenChange.
findings.fix: Pass `handleOnly` to that Drawer.Root (MessagesMobile.tsx:1006). vaul's Content then skips onPress and onDrag (:1468, :1500), and since ConversationView renders no Drawer.Handle, swipe-to-close is gone and Back still closes. This also stops the isDragging/scroll-lock re-render churn on every tap (:939-941). Alternative: keep swipe-back only from the header by putting `data-vaul-no-drag` on the message-list div (:1181) and the <form> (:1270), which shouldDrag honours at :981.
findings.risk: Low to medium. It removes the swipe-right-to-go-back gesture, which the founder may rely on.

findings.title: vaul's iOS scroll-lock focuses inputs itself on touchend, with no movement check
findings.symptom: A brush or drag across the composer strip opens the keyboard, and with the 14.5px textarea that means zoom, even though the user did not tap to type.
findings.root_cause: While a modal vaul drawer is open on iOS, usePreventScroll installs document capture listeners. onTouchEnd calls preventDefault() and target.focus() for any input or textarea that is not already focused. It never checks whether the touch moved. The composer is outside the message-list scroller and under the drawer's touch-action:none, so iOS never pans there and never sends pointercancel. The pointerup therefore runs vaul's onRelease, which sets isDragging false, and the listener is back in place before touchend reaches the textarea.
findings.evidence: node_modules/vaul/dist/index.mjs:939-941 usePreventScroll isDisabled only when not open, dragging, not modal, justReleased, !hasBeenOpened, !repositionInputs or !disablePreventScroll (disablePreventScroll defaults to true, so the lock stays on, :879). :216-230 onTouchEnd focuses the input; :274-283 listeners on document (capture, passive:false); :62 touch-action:none on the drawer. MessagesMobile.tsx:1270-1323 composer <form> and <textarea> inside Drawer.Content.
findings.fix: Fixing the first finding (16px) removes the zoom half. To stop the unwanted keyboard, pass `repositionInputs={false}` to the ConversationView Drawer.Root (MessagesMobile.tsx:1006). That disables usePreventScroll (:940), which a full-height right drawer does not need. Radix's RemoveScroll (react-dialog index.mjs:108) and vaul's body position:fixed (:787) still lock the page behind it.
findings.risk: Medium. iOS keyboard and scroll behaviour inside the drawer changes, so it needs a device test before shipping.

findings.title: (Low / mostly ruled out) SSR renders the desktop iframe branch first on a full page load
findings.symptom: On a cold load of /messages (refresh, home-screen launch, external link), a desktop layout flashes before the phone UI. This could read as a jump in scale.
findings.root_cause: useIsMobile's server snapshot is always false, so the SSR HTML is CampusAppShell plus the desktop messages.html iframe until hydration swaps to MobileShell. messages.html has 13px inputs and focus() calls. Focus inside an iframe without a user gesture should not raise the iOS keyboard, so this is unlikely to cause the zoom. Client-side navigation from the tab bar skips it entirely.
findings.evidence: src/lib/use-is-mobile.ts getServerSnapshot returns false; src/app/messages/MessagesSwitch.tsx:26-58 (desktop branch renders the iframe at 100vh); public/html/messages.html:6 viewport meta (ignored inside an iframe), :77/:85/:192 13px inputs, :1751/:2497/:3122 .focus(). MobileTabBar uses plain <Link>s (MobileTabBar.tsx:139-151).
findings.fix: No zoom fix needed. If the flash matters, render nothing on /messages until mounted, instead of the desktop branch.

phone_messages_react_lens.not_verified:
Nothing was tested on an iPhone. There was no device, no signed-in session, and starting a dev server was not allowed. Every iOS behaviour here comes from reading the code plus WebKit and CSS-Tricks documentation.

Specific points not confirmed:
- Whether iOS Safari sends pointerdown when a touch stops a momentum scroll, which the long-press "catch a flick" case depends on.
- Whether a fast flick delivers more than 10 px of pointermove before iOS fires pointercancel, which the vaul close-on-scroll case depends on. The same goes for whether iOS then still sends the trailing click that would open another thread.
- Whether the ComposeOverlay's 60 ms-delayed focus() raises the keyboard, and so zooms, on the founder's iOS version. I believe WebKit carries the user gesture into short timers, but did not check that.
- Whether vaul's touch-action:none stops pinch-out on the header and composer strips.
- Whether WebKit resets touch-action at a scroll container. That decides if `html { touch-action: manipulation }` alone reaches the message list.

Not done:
- Did not query the database for how many of the founder's DMs contain photos, videos or shared posts, which would show how much 5b62ff5's wider long-press area matters in practice.
- Did not read CampusMobile.tsx, which shares ConversationView. The member-sheet code at MessagesMobile.tsx:2310-2580 was only grepped: no inputs and no pointer or touch handlers found.
- Ruled out by code, not on device: open or close focus traps (vaul autoFocus is false; Radix sends close-focus to a trigger that does not exist); onPointerDown, onTouchStart or onMouseDown on thread rows, tabs or header buttons (all are onClick); Radix touch dismiss (it waits for the click); CustomCursor (it exits on coarse pointers); ToastHost (its container has pointerEvents none); text-size-adjust (Tailwind preflight sets it). interactive-widget is a Chromium feature, so its absence should not matter on iOS; that was not checked either.

phone_messages_ios_lens.summary:
Both symptoms have iOS causes I can trace to specific code. I found them by reading the code and WebKit's source and measuring the live viewport tag. Nothing was reproduced on a phone.

ZOOM. iOS Safari zooms in whenever you focus a text field whose font is under 16px, and it never zooms back out on its own. WebKit's zoom is exactly 16 divided by the font size. The site's viewport tag sets no zoom limit; I checked the live one: `width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover`.
- The Messages composer is 14.5px.
- The new-message search is 15px. It focuses itself 60 ms after the pencil tap, and WebKit treats a timer fired within 1 s of a tap as part of that tap. So the keyboard opens and the page zooms without the founder touching the field.
- At least 11 other phone fields on Campus, Network, Profile and the post viewer are also under 16px.
- A zoom picked up anywhere probably carries into Messages, because moving between tabs doesn't reload the page. That would explain "sometimes when I open messages it zooms in".
- Once the page is off its starting zoom, WebKit turns double-tap-to-zoom back on (verified in its source). No element in the app opts out with `touch-action: manipulation`, so the zoom tends to stick and grow.

UNINTENDED ACTIONS. Four causes, most likely first:
1. **Reaction long-press.** Pressing a message for 360 ms opens the reaction picker. A thumb resting still, or the touch that stops a fling, fires it, because nothing cancels it until the finger moves 10px. Session 57 (5b62ff5) made this more likely: it spread the same handler from the text bubble onto photos, videos and 260px-wide shared-post cards. The picker also closes on the first touch without swallowing the tap that follows. So "tap elsewhere to close" can open a shared post, toggle a reaction, or open the More sheet.
2. **The conversation screen can be dragged.** It's a vaul drawer that slides in from the right, and vaul lets side drawers drag from anywhere. Any leftward or >10px rightward drift moves the whole screen, and a quick rightward flick closes the chat. vaul's own CSS gives the drawer `touch-action: none`, so on the header and composer every finger drift goes to the drag.
3. **Screen jumps on every tap.** Every touch inside that drawer switches vaul's scroll lock off and back on, which scrolls the page to the top on release. With the keyboard up, the chat jumps under the finger, and the lock is off exactly while the finger is down, so the page behind can bounce.
4. **Text selection and link previews.** Only the bubbles block iOS text selection and the long-press link menu. Sender names, the header link and the tab bar links don't, which is the likely "select".

Minimal fixes:
- Make every phone text field 16px: change 2 lines in MessagesMobile, or add one global `!important` rule, since each field sets its size inline.
- Add `handleOnly` (or `dismissible={false}`) to the conversation's `Drawer.Root`.
- Long-press: wait about 500 ms, cancel it on scroll, and close the picker in a way that swallows the tap.
- On the message list: `touch-action: manipulation`, `overscroll-behavior: contain`, and callout/select none.

Ruled out:
- The old 350 ms delayed click: WebKit doesn't delay taps at normal zoom on this page, and the only tap-through is the picker's (cause 1).
- Mouse events faked from touches: CustomCursor exits early on touch screens and Messages has no mouse handlers.
- vaul/Radix grabbing focus when a sheet opens or closes.
- 100vh vs 100dvh: the phone layout already uses dvh.
- Text-size-adjust: Tailwind's reset sets it to 100%.

findings.title: [Zoom #1] Every Messages text field is under 16px and the viewport sets no zoom limit, so iOS focus-zooms, including on the new-message search's own autofocus
findings.symptom: Page zooms in when the founder taps the composer, or immediately when he taps the New message pencil; the zoom stays after the keyboard closes and is still there when he comes back to Messages.
findings.root_cause: WebKit zooms to a focused editable element by scale = 16 / fontSize, clamped only by the page's maximum scale. Our viewport has no maximum-scale. The composer textarea is 14.5px (zoom 1.10x) and the compose search input is 15px (zoom 1.067x). ComposeOverlay focuses the search input from a 60ms setTimeout. WebKit forwards the triggering tap's user-gesture token to timers for up to 1s, so the keyboard opens and the zoom fires without the user touching the field. iOS never zooms back out on blur. Fields under 16px on other phone screens can leave the page zoomed before Messages is opened, because Next.js soft navigation keeps the same document.
findings.evidence: src/components/mobile/MessagesMobile.tsx:1292-1323 textarea with fontSize 14.5 at :1318. MessagesMobile.tsx:2775-2795 search input with fontSize 15 at :2791. MessagesMobile.tsx:2620-2625 `window.setTimeout(() => inputRef.current?.focus(), 60)`; its comment says the delay is 'so iOS Safari honors the focus'. MessagesMobile.tsx:932 re-focuses the textarea after every send. The only field at 16px or more is the group-rename input (17px, :2166). src/app/layout.tsx:27-32 viewport has only width, initialScale and viewportFit. MEASURED: curl with an iPhone user agent on https://www.connectvibe.app/messages (redirected to /auth/login, same root layout) returns `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover"/>`. WebKit WKWebViewIOS.mm (main): `const double webViewStandardFontSize = 16; scale = clampTo<double>(webViewStandardFontSize / fontSize, minimumScale, maximumScale);`. WebKit UserGestureIndicator.h: `static constexpr Seconds maximumIntervalForUserGestureForwarding { 1_s };`, and DOMTimer.cpp forwards the token unless it has expired past that interval. Git: the 14.5px composer dates from c2206cd and the autofocus from bb1a27f; maximumScale/userScalable never appear in the layout.tsx history. Audit of other phone fields under 16px: CampusMobile.tsx:1473 (14), :1920 (14), :2875 (15); NetworkMobile.tsx:391 (15); ProfileMobile.tsx:1380 (13), :1594 (14), :3592 (14), :4096 (14), :4143 (14), :4746 (13); PostViewerMobile.tsx:754 (14); SharePostSheet.tsx:290, :387 (13.5). Ruled out as zoom sources: vaul prevents Radix's open auto-focus by default (node_modules/vaul/dist/index.mjs:1476-1481; autoFocus=false at :879), and Radix's modal Dialog on close focuses only the trigger (node_modules/@radix-ui/react-dialog/dist/index.mjs:145-148), which does not exist here because no Drawer.Trigger is used. Tailwind preflight sets -webkit-text-size-adjust:100% (globals.css:1 imports tailwindcss; node_modules/tailwindcss/preflight.css:31).
findings.fix: Minimal fix for Messages: MessagesMobile.tsx:1318 fontSize 14.5 -> 16 and :2791 15 -> 16 (trim padding if the height matters). Phone-wide fix, one rule in globals.css: `@media (max-width: 899px) { input:not([type=checkbox]):not([type=radio]):not([type=range]):not([type=file]), textarea, select { font-size: 16px !important; } }`. The !important is required because every field sets fontSize inline. Do not use maximumScale:1 in layout.tsx: it stops the focus zoom on iOS but disables pinch-zoom on Android Chrome, an accessibility regression. Optionally drop the ComposeOverlay autofocus (:2620-2625) so the keyboard does not open uninvited.
findings.risk: A global !important font rule will enlarge every phone field currently sized 13-15px, so a few fields may reflow. The two-line Messages change carries no such risk.

findings.title: [Zoom #2] Once zoomed, WebKit re-enables double-tap zoom and nothing opts out; vaul's touch-action:none also blocks pinching back out on the chat header and composer
findings.symptom: After the first zoom, the screen keeps zooming further on quick successive taps, taps feel slower, and pinching out does not work on parts of the conversation screen.
findings.root_cause: WebKit disables double-tap gestures for width=device-width pages only while the current scale equals the initial scale. After any focus zoom they come back on. No element in the app sets touch-action: manipulation. The message list is a scroll container, and WebKit resets touch-action at scroll containers, so double-tap zoom is live there even inside the vaul drawer. The thread list (the page scrolls the root) is unprotected too. Meanwhile the drawer's header and composer inherit vaul's injected touch-action:none, which also disables pinch-zoom there, so the zoomed state is hard to undo.
findings.evidence: WebKit WKWebViewIOS.mm `_allowsDoubleTapGestures` (quoted) ends with `// We'll enable double tap zoom whenever we're not at the actual initial scale. return !WebKit::scalesAreEssentiallyEqual(contentZoomScale(self), _perProcessState.initialScaleFactor);`. WebKit StyleAdjuster.cpp computeUsedTouchAction: `bool hasDefaultTouchBehavior = isScrollableOverflow(style.overflowX()) || isScrollableOverflow(style.overflowY()); if (hasDefaultTouchBehavior) usedTouchAction = ComputedStyle::initialTouchAction();`. MEASURED: `grep -c touch-action src/app/globals.css` = 0, and MessagesMobile.tsx has no touchAction. MessagesMobile.tsx:1181-1194 message list is overflowY:auto with no touchAction; :359-366 main has no touchAction. node_modules/vaul/dist/index.mjs:62 injects `[data-vaul-drawer]{touch-action:none;...}`. Git history shows touch-action only in clips and profile-edit features.
findings.fix: The Zoom #1 fix is the real fix: at initial scale WebKit already disables double-tap. As defense in depth, add `touchAction: "manipulation"` to the message-list div style (MessagesMobile.tsx:1189-1194) and `html { touch-action: manipulation; }` in globals.css. It must be set on the scroll container itself, because scroll containers reset inherited touch-action.
findings.risk: touch-action: manipulation keeps pan and pinch and only removes double-tap zoom, so the risk is low.

findings.title: [Taps #1] The reaction long-press fires at 360ms under a resting or scroll-stopping thumb, on the much larger media and card targets Session 57 added; the picker's pointerdown dismiss lets that tap click through
findings.symptom: The emoji picker pops up while he is scrolling or just resting a thumb. Tapping away to close it opens a shared post, toggles a reaction or opens the More sheet. Reacting to an older message yanks the list to the bottom.
findings.root_cause: pointerdown starts a 360ms timer. Only a move over 10px, pointerup, pointercancel or pointerleave cancels it. On iOS a stationary finger sends no pointermove or pointercancel until a native pan starts. That covers a thumb resting before a scroll, and the touch that stops a momentum fling (iOS still delivers the touch but suppresses the click). 360ms is shorter than UIKit's 0.5s default long-press. vaul calls setPointerCapture on the pointerdown target, so pointerleave cannot fire mid-gesture and the onPointerLeave cancel is dead. Session 57 moved the handlers from the single text bubble onto photos, videos, 260px-wide shared-post cards and notice tiles. ReactionPicker closes on a document 'pointerdown' and never swallows the click that follows, so iOS still clicks the tapped element.
findings.evidence: MessagesMobile.tsx:3005-3020 startLongPress (timer 360 at :3019). :3023-3028 10px cancel. :3034-3053 pressHandlers (pointer down/move/up/cancel/leave, contextmenu, onClickCapture guard). The handlers are spread at :3122 (notice tile), :3146 (text), :3182 (video), :3206 (photo) and :3251 (the shared-post Link, width 260 at :3254). `git show 5b62ff5` adds `const pressHandlers = {...}` and deletes the handlers from the lone bubble div (`-onPointerDown={(e) => startLongPress(...)}` in the final hunk). ReactionPicker :3589-3604 binds `document.addEventListener("pointerdown", handler)` and calls onClose() without preventing the later click. By contrast, Radix defers touch outside-dismiss to the click (node_modules/@radix-ui/react-dismissable-layer/dist/index.mjs:153-156). vaul setPointerCapture: node_modules/vaul/dist/index.mjs:968. List jump: toggleReaction calls setMessages (:940), and the effect at :876-880 sets scrollTop = scrollHeight on every messages change. Long-press origin: 52343e8.
findings.fix: (a) Raise the timer to about 500ms (:3019). (b) Cancel pending long-presses on list scroll: in the list's onScroll (:1183-1188), record a 'scrolled at' time in a shared ref and have the timer callback bail if a scroll happened after its pointerdown, or clear timers via context. (c) In ReactionPicker, dismiss from a capture-phase `click` listener that calls preventDefault() and stopPropagation() when the target is outside, instead of the pointerdown listener, so the dismissing tap cannot activate what is underneath. (d) Make the :876-880 effect scroll only when a message is appended and pinnedToBottomRef is true, not on reaction updates.
findings.risk: A longer press makes reactions slightly slower to open. The capture-phase click dismiss must still let emoji taps inside the picker through (keep the contains() check).

findings.title: [Taps #2] The conversation is a vaul direction="right" drawer: it drags from anywhere, and a quick rightward flick closes the chat
findings.symptom: While scrolling or touching the header or composer, the whole conversation slides sideways, and sometimes the chat closes on its own mid-gesture.
findings.root_cause: vaul's shouldDrag returns true unconditionally for left and right drawers. That skips the scroll-position, text-selection and opening-animation guards vertical drawers get. Content's isDeltaInDirection latches 'drag allowed' on the first move with any leftward component, or more than 10px rightward, and never re-checks vertical dominance. On release, rightward velocity over 0.4 px/ms, or a translate of 25% of the width, closes the drawer: onOpenChange(false) calls onClose and the conversation unmounts. vaul's CSS puts touch-action:none on the drawer, so on the header, composer and error banner the browser never pans and every drift is routed into the JS drag. Inside the list, native scroll wins, but the pre-pan moves still reach vaul. Then pointercancel is followed by pointerout, and vaul's onPointerOut runs onRelease with the last move, so a fast diagonal flick can translate and close the drawer. The same component serves org channels in CampusMobile.
findings.evidence:
MessagesMobile.tsx:1006-1010 `<Drawer.Root open direction="right" onOpenChange=...>` with no handleOnly or dismissible. In node_modules/vaul/dist/index.mjs:
- :984-986 `if (direction === 'right' || direction === 'left') { return true; }` inside shouldDrag
- :1419-1441 isDeltaInDirection (latches wasBeyondThePointRef)
- :1505 swipeStartThreshold 10 for touch
- :446-447 VELOCITY_THRESHOLD 0.4 and CLOSE_THRESHOLD 0.25
- :1252-1271 release logic: reset if moved left, close if velocity > 0.4 or translate ≥ 25%
- :1522-1525 onPointerOut calls handleOnPointerUp(lastKnownPointerEventRef.current)
- :62 `[data-vaul-drawer]{touch-action:none}`

The list resets touch-action because it is a scroll container (MessagesMobile.tsx:1189-1194; WebKit computeUsedTouchAction). Reused at CampusMobile.tsx:493. Drawer origin: 6119831.
findings.fix: Minimal: add `handleOnly` to the Drawer.Root at MessagesMobile.tsx:1006. vaul's Content onPointerDown and onPointerMove then return early (vaul index.mjs:1468 and :1500), so onPress and onDrag never run. There is no Drawer.Handle, so the chat is simply not swipe-draggable, and Back still closes it. `dismissible={false}` also stops onPress (vaul :955). Longer term, render the conversation as a plain fixed full-screen view, as ComposeOverlay (:2690-2702) and GroupSettingsView (:2055-2068) already do.
findings.risk: Removes swipe-to-close, which is likely undiscoverable anyway; Back remains. Verify CampusMobile org channels still close correctly.

findings.title: [Taps #3] vaul switches its iOS scroll lock off and on for every touch in the conversation and calls window.scrollTo on each tap
findings.symptom: The chat bounces behind itself when he scrolls at the bottom, and with the keyboard open the content jumps under his finger on every tap, so taps feel like they land somewhere unexpected.
findings.root_cause: onPress calls setIsDragging(true) on every pointerdown inside the drawer, and onRelease sets it false. isDragging is part of usePreventScroll's disable condition, and that hook runs as a layout effect. So each touch tears the lock down: it removes the capture-phase touchstart, touchmove, touchend and focus listeners and the window-scroll listener, then calls window.scrollTo(savedX, savedY). Each release re-installs it with window.scrollTo(0,0) plus a scroll listener that forces 0,0. The lock is therefore off exactly while a finger is down, and its edge preventDefault never applies. The message list is always pinned to the bottom and has no overscroll-behavior, so the first downward drag chains into a page rubber-band. With the keyboard up, iOS has scrolled the window to reveal the composer, and every tap release inside the conversation scrolls it back to 0. While re-installed, its touchend handler also preventDefaults taps on inputs and focuses them itself with a translateY(-2000px) trick. Separately, on Safari vaul sets body to position:fixed while the drawer is open.
findings.evidence:
In node_modules/vaul/dist/index.mjs:
- :959 setIsDragging(true) in onPress, and :1226 setIsDragging(false) in onRelease
- :939-941 `usePreventScroll({ isDisabled: !isOpen || isDragging || ... })`
- :138 useIsomorphicLayoutEffect
- :184-289 preventScrollMobileSafari: edge preventDefault at :211-213, input touchend trick at :216-230, onWindowScroll → scrollTo(0,0) at :261-265, scrollTo(0,0) at :273, restore with scrollTo(scrollX, scrollY) at :284-289
- :770-877 usePositionFixed, with body position fixed at :787

MessagesMobile.tsx:1189-1194 list style has no overscrollBehavior, and there is no overscroll rule anywhere in MessagesMobile.tsx or globals.css (grep). :876-880 pins the list to the bottom.
findings.fix: The `handleOnly` (or dismissible={false}) change from Taps #2 stops onPress, so isDragging never toggles and the lock stays steady for the drawer's lifetime. Also add `overscrollBehavior: "contain"` to the list at MessagesMobile.tsx:1189-1194.
findings.risk: Once the lock is permanently active, vaul's input touchend and focus trick runs on every composer tap. That is vaul's intended behavior, but re-test typing on a device.

findings.title: [Taps #4] iOS text selection and link-preview callouts are only suppressed on bubbles, not the rest of the chat or the tab bar
findings.symptom: A resting finger starts the blue text selection, or a long press pops an iOS link preview of a profile or tab page.
findings.root_cause: Only the long-pressable bubble, media and card surfaces set -webkit-touch-callout:none and user-select:none. vaul's own user-select:none for drawers sits inside @media (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine), so it does not apply on an iPhone. Sender-name rows, the header title, the empty-state text and timestamps are selectable. Links without callout:none show the iOS preview on long-press: the header peer link, the tab bar links, the empty-state Find people link, and the View profile sheet rows.
findings.evidence: MessagesMobile.tsx:3092-3099 pressStyle is the only place that sets callout and selection off; the single WebkitTouchCallout occurrence in the file is :3094. Unprotected: sender row :3427-3471; header Link :1101-1116; EmptyState Link :779-794; SheetRow Link :1762-1768. src/components/mobile/MobileTabBar.tsx:138-151 tab Links are styled by .vibe-mobile-tab at src/app/globals.css:2590-2607, which sets only -webkit-tap-highlight-color. vaul CSS at node_modules/vaul/dist/index.mjs:62: `@media (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine){[data-vaul-drawer]{user-select:none}}`.
findings.fix: Add `WebkitUserSelect: "none", userSelect: "none", WebkitTouchCallout: "none"` to the message-list div (:1189-1194) and the conversation header (:1034-1050), but not the textarea. Add `-webkit-touch-callout: none;` to .vibe-mobile-tab in globals.css:2590-2607.
findings.risk: Users can no longer select or copy message text. Bubbles already block it, so nothing is lost there.

phone_messages_ios_lens.not_verified:
- Nothing was run on an iPhone or in the iOS Simulator. Every on-device behavior is inferred from repo code plus WebKit main-branch source on GitHub, which may differ from the founder's iOS version.
- Checked against WebKit source: the double-tap rule, the 16px focus-zoom formula, the scroll-container touch-action reset, and the 1 s timer gesture forwarding.
- Assumed, not confirmed:
  - iOS keeps the page zoom across Next.js soft navigations; this is the "sometimes when I open Messages" explanation.
  - iOS delivers pointerdown for a touch that stops a momentum scroll while suppressing its click.
  - UIKit's long-press default is 0.5 s.
  - Double-tap being on brings back a delay on single taps.
- WebKit's WebPage::commitPotentialTap couldn't be fetched (the file was truncated). So I can't say whether vaul's per-tap scrollTo jumps make iOS drop a tap or click the wrong element.
- I didn't read the separate fetch gesture window (maximumIntervalForUserGestureForwardingForFetch). So it's unknown whether the focus() after send at MessagesMobile.tsx:932 reopens the keyboard.
- The fast-diagonal-flick close inside a scrolling list (pointercancel, then pointerout, then onRelease) is reasoned from vaul's code, not reproduced.
- The production /messages fetch landed on the login page (same root layout). The viewport tag was measured there, not on a signed-in Messages page.
- No SQL was run: thread lengths wouldn't change the ranking, because the message list resets touch-action whether or not it overflows.
- I didn't audit the static public/html/messages.html (desktop iframe only) or the iOS left-edge back swipe. The conversation isn't a history entry, so that swipe likely leaves /messages entirely; unverified.
- I made no file edits and ran only read-only git commands. The Session 57 diff was saved to the scratchpad for reading only.

desktop_perf_cursor.summary:
Setup: the founder's signed-in headed gstack Chromium 145 on a MacBook Pro with a 120 Hz Liquid Retina XDR display, viewport 1440x900, dpr 1. At the end the browser is back on https://www.connectvibe.app/campus at 1200x745 (checked: "1200x745 /campus"). The repo is untouched (`git status` clean). Scratch scripts are only in the scratchpad.

What the numbers say:

1. **The power state, not the site, set the first frame rate.** On the first pass the Mac was at 2% battery and discharging. /campus ran at exactly 30 fps (rAF p50 33.3 ms, 90 of 90 frames over 20 ms, no long tasks). After it was plugged in:
   - a blank file:// control page ran at 120 fps (p50 8.3 ms);
   - all four pages ran at 120 fps.

2. **Plugged in at 120 Hz, I measured no jank on any page.** Every run below had 0 frames over 20 ms, max 9.4 ms, and 0 long tasks:
   - /campus: idle, programmatic scroll at 1200 px/s over 1800 px, synthetic mousemove once per frame, and 12 real hovers across the nav and the feed;
   - /network: idle, scroll and hover;
   - /html/profile.html?app=1: idle, scroll and hover.
   The only long frames were on /messages (229 and 178 ms), during my hover chain into the iframe. They carry no script or style attribution and happened while a Playwright hover timed out, so they are probably the test harness.

3. **The lag you can feel is the cursor itself.** On React pages the native cursor is hidden (globals.css:1559-1564), so the coral dot is the pointer.
   - The dot trails the hand by 42 ms in steady motion and needs 83 ms to cover 90% of a jump.
   - The ring trails the hand by 72 ms and needs 166 ms to cover 90% of a jump, 266 ms to 99%.
   - The cause is an 80 ms CSS transform transition on both the dot and the ring (globals.css:1579 and 1593), stacked on a per-frame lerp of 0.22.
   - At 60 Hz this becomes 233 ms (simulated). At 30 fps it was 400 ms, measured on battery.
   - For comparison, the static profile page's ring reaches 90% in 58 ms on the same machine, and its dot is instant.
   - A simulation of the lerp plus the per-frame transition restart reproduces the live data: the 30 fps curve to three decimals ([0.001,0.13,0.285,0.428,…] measured vs [0,0.13,0.285,0.427,…] simulated) and the 120 Hz frame count exactly (20 frames).

4. **Cursor mechanics, all four implementations:**
   - None of them uses React state. All write `style.transform` directly.
   - All use a 2D `translate()`, not top/left. There is no translate3d.
   - All re-request animation frames forever, even when the mouse is still. Measured: about 120 rAF callbacks per second on every page. In 5 s of idle this loop was the only rAF site. There were zero setTimeout/setInterval registrations and zero fetches.
   - Ring follow factors per frame: React 0.22 (plus the 80 ms transition), profile and standalone messages 0.28, onboarding 0.18.
   - Time to cover 90% of a jump at 60 Hz: React 233 ms (167 ms without the transition), profile/messages 117 ms, onboarding 200 ms.

5. **/messages runs one cursor, not two.**
   - The parent's React dot and ring are `display:block`.
   - The iframe's `#cursor` and `#cursorRing` are `display:none` (messages.html:1078-1080).
   - The iframe body has `cursor:none` (messages.html:36).
   - The iframe registered 0 rAF and 0 timers in 4.4 s.
   - The iframe forwards mouse moves to the parent by postMessage (messages.html:1081-1086, CustomCursor.tsx:108-133).

6. **Heavy glass is present but cost nothing measurable on this machine.**
   - /campus: 10 visible backdrop-filter layers covering 71% of the viewport. The largest is a 600,534 px² `blur(28px) saturate(180%)` GLASS_SURFACE, 46% of the viewport.
   - /network: 11 layers, 58.7% of the viewport.
   - Profile: 31 in the DOM but only 2 visible (11%). /messages: none.
   - Infinite animations are transform/opacity only: 3 on /campus and /network (the Otto orb), 7 on profile.
   - Frame pacing during scrolling stayed at 120 fps.

7. **Load.** The 120 Hz runs used a warm cache:

   | Page | DCL | Load | FCP | JS (gz / raw) |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | /campus | 716 ms | 1343 ms | 792 ms | 17 scripts, 406 KB / 1344 KB |
   | /messages (parent) | 399 ms | 1094 ms | 508 ms | 13 scripts, 323 KB / 1028 KB |
   | /messages iframe | 702 ms | not recorded | not recorded | doc 48 KB gz / 176 KB raw, plus 7 scripts, 48 KB / 166 KB |
   | /network | 459 ms | 598 ms | 488 ms | 11 scripts, 303 KB / 959 KB |
   | profile.html | 701 ms | 1007 ms | 508 ms | 12 scripts, 95 KB / 386 KB (HTML is 425 KB decoded) |

   The largest /campus chunk is 134 KB gz / 421 KB raw. Profile includes pdf.js at 313 KB raw, loaded eagerly. The one cold /campus load, on battery, transferred 139 KB of JS with DCL 2201 ms and FCP 2288 ms.

**Recommended tuning, applied the same way everywhere:**
- Remove `transform 0.08s ease-out` from `.vibe-cursor--dot` and `.vibe-cursor--ring`.
- Replace the per-frame lerp with a time-based exponential follow, `a = 1 - Math.exp(-dt/17)`, with TAU = 17 ms. The ring then covers 90% of a jump in about 39 ms in continuous time. Simulated with frame steps: 42 ms at 120 Hz (k=0.387), 50 ms at 60 Hz (k=0.625), and still about 40 ms at 30 fps (k=0.86). Steady-motion trail is 10-13 ms.
- Keep the dot a direct write in the mousemove handler.
- Use subpixel `translate3d` and drop `Math.round`.
- Stop the loop once the ring is within 0.2 px of the pointer, and restart it from mousemove.
- Apply this to src/components/CustomCursor.tsx, public/html/profile.html:3925-3930, public/html/messages.html:1088-1090 and public/html/onboarding.html:703-706.

findings.title: React custom cursor: an 80 ms CSS transform transition on both dot and ring, stacked on a 0.22 lerp, makes the pointer itself lag
findings.symptom: On /campus, /messages, /network and every React route, the coral dot (the only visible pointer) trails the hand and the ring trails much further. This is the 'ring lags a little too much' complaint and a big part of 'the desktop site seems laggy'.
findings.root_cause: src/app/globals.css:1579 gives `.vibe-cursor--dot` `transition: transform 0.08s ease-out` and globals.css:1593 gives `.vibe-cursor--ring` `transition: border-color 0.18s ease, transform 0.08s ease-out`. The dot's transform is written on every mousemove (CustomCursor.tsx:59-64) and the ring's on every frame (CustomCursor.tsx:87-92, `rx += (mx - rx) * 0.22`). Each write restarts an 80 ms ease-out transition, which acts as a second smoothing filter on the ring and turns the dot, documented as 'snaps to the pointer' (CustomCursor.tsx:6), into an eased follower. The native cursor is hidden (globals.css:1559-1564), so there is nothing that doesn't lag.
findings.evidence: Live, 120 Hz, /campus and /messages parent, identical results. Computed dot transition: 'transform 0.08s ease-out, background 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s'. Computed ring transition: 'border-color 0.18s, transform 0.08s ease-out'. Jump test (synthetic mousemove from (400,400) to (1000,650), positions read from computed transforms each frame): dot 90% at 10 frames = 83 ms; ring 50% at 9 frames, 90% at 20 frames = 166 ms, 99% at 32 frames = 266 ms. Sweep at 1000 px/s: dot 42 ms behind the pointer, ring 72 ms behind the pointer, ring 30 px behind the dot. The same test on battery at 30 fps: ring 90% at 12 frames = 400 ms, dot 90% at 5 frames = 166 ms. A simulation of lerp 0.22 plus an 80 ms ease-out restarted every frame reproduces the 30 fps curve to 3 decimals (measured [0.001,0.13,0.285,0.428,0.548,0.643,0.723,0.782] vs simulated [0,0.13,0.285,0.427,0.547,0.644,0.721,0.782]) and the 120 Hz frame count (20 vs 20). Simulated at 60 Hz: ring 90% in 233 ms. The deployed chunk 2vtq64sdzvo_j.js line 2 col ~16193 contains `u+=(o-u)*.22 ... requestAnimationFrame(e)`, confirming prod runs this code.
findings.fix: Delete `transform 0.08s ease-out` from both rules and keep only the colour transitions: dot `transition: background 0.15s ease, box-shadow 0.15s ease;`, ring `transition: border-color 0.18s ease;`. Simulated effect at 120 Hz before any retuning: dot lag 83 ms to 0 ms; ring 90% time 166 ms to 83 ms. Then apply the time-based follow in the next finding.
findings.risk: Low. The only visible change is the dot snapping exactly to the pointer. prefers-reduced-motion already strips these transitions (globals.css:1605-1610).

findings.title: All four cursor rings use a slow per-frame lerp, so the lag depends on refresh rate and differs between surfaces
findings.symptom: The ring trails 2x more on 60 Hz monitors than on the MacBook's 120 Hz panel, and 4x more when Chrome drops to 30 fps. Moving between /campus (React) and the profile page (static) changes how the cursor feels.
findings.root_cause: Every implementation advances the ring by a fixed fraction per animation frame rather than per unit of time. React uses 0.22 (CustomCursor.tsx:88-89); profile.html uses 0.28 (profile.html:3930); standalone messages.html uses 0.28 (messages.html:1090); onboarding.html uses 0.18 (onboarding.html:705). Frames to cover 90% of a jump = ln(0.1)/ln(1-k): 9.27 frames for 0.22, 7.01 for 0.28, 11.6 for 0.18.
findings.evidence: Implied time to 90% at 60 Hz: 0.22 gives 167 ms (233 ms with the React CSS transition), 0.28 gives 117 ms, 0.18 gives 200 ms. At 120 Hz: 83 / 58 / 100 ms. At 30 fps: 333 / 233 / 400 ms. Live, 120 Hz, /html/profile.html?app=1 (static, k=0.28, no transform transition): ring fractions [0.28,0.481,0.627,0.732,0.807,0.86,0.9,0.928], 90% at 7 frames = 58 ms, ring 21 px behind the dot at 1000 px/s (simulated 21.4), dot instant (1 frame). The React ring on the same machine took 166 ms, 2.9x slower. On battery (2%, discharging), /campus rAF ran at p50 33.3 ms (30 fps) and the React ring took 400 ms to 90%.
findings.fix: Use one time-based follow in all four files. Keep `mx, my, rx, ry`; in mousemove set mx/my, write `dot.style.transform = `translate3d(${mx-4}px,${my-4}px,0)``, then call `kick()`. Loop: `const TAU=17; let last=0, raf=0; function tick(t){ const dt = last ? Math.min(t-last, 64) : 16.7; last = t; const a = 1 - Math.exp(-dt/TAU); rx += (mx-rx)*a; ry += (my-ry)*a; ring.style.transform = `translate3d(${rx-14}px,${ry-14}px,0)`; if (Math.abs(mx-rx)+Math.abs(my-ry) > 0.2) raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick); else { raf = 0; last = 0; } } function kick(){ if(!raf) raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick); }`. TAU = 17 ms gives a continuous 90% time of 39 ms. Simulated with frame steps: 42 ms at 120 Hz (k=0.387, 5 frames), 50 ms at 60 Hz (k=0.625, 3 frames), about 40 ms at 30 fps (k=0.86). Steady-motion trail is 10-13 ms. For more visible trailing, TAU = 20 ms gives 46 ms continuous (50 ms at both 60 and 120 Hz). Static profile and messages keep their `-14` inside the lerp (`rx += (mx-rx-14)*a`), so use the same TAU with their offset convention. Drop `Math.round` (CustomCursor.tsx:90, profile.html:3930, messages.html:1090) to avoid 1 px stepping.
findings.risk: Low. Each loop is under 10 lines. The React cursor also receives iframe moves through applyPosition (CustomCursor.tsx:59-64, 115-118), so call kick() there too, or the ring will stop following over the /messages iframe.

findings.title: Cursor rAF loops run forever, about 120 wakeups per second on every page even when the mouse is still
findings.symptom: Idle pages never go quiet: a style write every frame and constant main-thread wakeups (a battery cost). This measured as no jank, but it is the only perpetual idle work on these pages.
findings.root_cause: All four ticks call requestAnimationFrame unconditionally: CustomCursor.tsx:87-92 (started at :145), profile.html:3930, messages.html:1090 (standalone only), onboarding.html:705-706.
findings.evidence: rAF/setTimeout/setInterval/fetch wrapped after load, then 5 s idle at 120 Hz. /campus: 621 rAF registrations in 5.17 s, all from `e (2vtq64sdzvo_j.js:2:16193)`, which is the CustomCursor tick. /network: 620 in 5.16 s, same site. /messages parent: 618 in 5.14 s, same site. The /messages iframe: 0 rAF and 0 timers in 4.4 s. profile.html: 612 in 5.09 s from `tick (profile.html:3930:130)`. Zero setTimeout/setInterval registrations and zero fetches in those windows. No long tasks or long animation frames in the idle windows.
findings.fix: Stop the loop when |mx-rx|+|my-ry| < 0.2 px and restart it from mousemove (and from CustomCursor's postMessage path) with kick(), as in the snippet in the previous finding. Also cancel the frame on unmount (already done at CustomCursor.tsx:148).
findings.risk: Very low. Forgetting to call kick() on the iframe-forwarded path would freeze the ring over /messages.

findings.title: On low battery the browser ran every page at 30 fps, which doubles or quadruples all frame-based motion
findings.symptom: On battery the whole site, including cursor trailing and scrolling, felt twice as slow as plugged in. The frame-based ring lerp makes this much more noticeable.
findings.root_cause: This is environmental. The Mac was at 2% battery, discharging ('Battery Warning: Final'). The exact 33.3 ms cadence with no long tasks points to a browser or OS frame cap such as Chrome's Energy Saver 30 fps mode, not page work. The code-side part is that the cursor lerps are per frame (see the refresh-rate finding above).
findings.evidence: First pass (battery 2%, discharging, per pmset and navigator.getBattery {level:0.02, charging:false}): /campus idle rAF n=90, p50 33.3, p95 34.8, all 90 frames over 20 ms, no long tasks or long animation frames in the window. Also, /campus React ring 90% took 12 frames = 400 ms. After the machine was plugged in (charging, 5-13%): blank file:// control page p50 8.3 ms (120 fps, 0 frames over 20 ms), and /campus idle p50 8.3 ms (120 fps).
findings.fix: No site-side fix beyond making the cursor time-based (see the refresh-rate finding above), which keeps the ring at about 40 ms even at 30 fps. When judging smoothness on battery, check Chrome's Performance > Energy Saver setting.

findings.title: Large backdrop-filter glass covers 59-71% of the viewport on /campus and /network, but no frame cost was measurable on this machine
findings.symptom: Not observed as frame drops on the M-series MacBook. It could cost frames on weaker GPUs (Intel iGPU, Windows laptops), which I did not test.
findings.root_cause: GLASS_SURFACE uses `blur(28px) saturate(180%)` on the main feed panel (src/app/campus/campus-home.tsx:178-188). DARK_GLASS_SURFACE uses `blur(28px) saturate(160%)` (campus-home.tsx:4128-4131) and is applied inside MouseSpotlight's 3D-tilting layer on event cards (campus-home.tsx:6781-6788; mouse-spotlight.tsx:74-93 tilt, :112-120 preserve-3d with a 380 ms transform transition). campus-home.tsx has 31 backdropFilter declarations. The Otto orb runs 3 infinite animations (campus-home.tsx:3198-3209).
findings.evidence: Computed-style scan at 1440x900. /campus: 10 backdrop-filter elements, all visible, 71% of the viewport; the largest is a div of 600,534 px² (46% of the viewport) with `blur(28px) saturate(1.8)`, then 146,718 px², div.otto-strip 75,110 px², nav#campus-tabs 72,540 px² `blur(20px) saturate(1.6)`. /network: 11 visible, 58.7% (five 134,862 px² cards). profile.html: 31 in the DOM, 2 visible, 11% area. /messages: 0 in the parent and 0 in the iframe. Running infinite animations (gstack's own injected shimmer excluded): /campus and /network 3 (otto-breath 2.8 s, otto-orbit-spin 8 s, otto-core-pulse 2.4 s, all transform/opacity); profile 7 (op-*/otto*, transform/opacity). will-change count 0 on React pages. Frame pacing at 120 Hz on /campus: scrolling 1200 px/s over 1800 px gave 360 frames, p50 8.3, p95 9.3, max 9.4, 0 over 20 ms. Synthetic mousemove and 12 real hovers (nav, feed, Otto corner) gave 0 over 20 ms. /network hover: 541 frames, 0 over 20 ms.
findings.fix: No change is needed for this machine. Test a weaker GPU first. If drops appear: reduce the blur radius on the full-height feed surface (for example 28px to 12-16px in GLASS_SURFACE), limit backdrop-filter to sticky chrome (tabs, search, header), and stop the Otto orb animations and the MouseSpotlight tilt on glass cards when offscreen or on low-power devices.
findings.risk: Visual change to the brand's glass look; only do it if a weaker-hardware test shows dropped frames.

findings.title: Three polling requests every 30 s on React pages; no measured frame cost
findings.symptom: Periodic network requests plus state updates; not observed as jank.
findings.root_cause: CampusBanner POSTs /api/me/heartbeat then GETs /api/stats/campus every 30 s and calls setStats on each response (campus-home.tsx:3232-3264). OttoCorner polls /api/me/notifications/count every 30 s (OttoCorner.tsx:12, :93-107) and calls setUnread/setUnreadMention.
findings.evidence: The browse network log on /campus showed 4 rounds of heartbeat, notifications/count and stats/campus about 30 s apart (for example page times 662518/662519/663464, 692519/692521/693223 ms). The fetch wrapper saw 0 fetches in each 5 s idle window. At 120 Hz there were no long tasks in any measured window. On battery there were unattributed long tasks up to 590 ms near a heartbeat at page time 632.4 s, but their long-animation-frame entries had no script attribution and the heartbeat due at about 602 s was missing (timers were delayed), so I treat those as the starved machine, not this code.
findings.fix: Not a lag fix. Optionally skip setStats and setUnread when the values have not changed, so a poll never re-renders CampusBanner or OttoCorner for nothing.

findings.title: profile.html loads pdf.js on every view and has a 275 ms long animation frame at load with 44 ms of forced layout
findings.symptom: A slower first paint and settle on the desktop profile. This happens once at load, not during use.
findings.root_cause: profile.html:19 loads `https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/pdf.js/3.11.174/pdf.min.js` (defer) unconditionally; the worker is set at profile.html:4667. The page also ships 425 KB of decoded HTML. A requestAnimationFrame callback during load forces style and layout.
findings.evidence: profile.html?app=1 at 120 Hz, warm cache: DCL 701 ms, load 1007 ms, FCP 508 ms, 12 scripts at 95 KB gz / 386 KB raw, of which pdf.min.js is 72 KB gz / 313 KB raw; document is 425 KB decoded. The load-time long animation frame at s=196 ms had d=275 ms, blocking 14 ms, a script from profile.html of 9 ms, and a FrameRequestCallback of 44 ms whose forcedStyleAndLayoutDuration was 44 ms. The function name was empty, so I did not identify it. For comparison, /campus warm load: DCL 716 ms, load 1343 ms, FCP 792 ms, 17 scripts at 406 KB gz / 1,344 KB raw (largest chunk 0ttg5tvb2exho.js 134 KB gz / 421 KB raw); the cold run on battery transferred 139 KB of JS with DCL 2201 ms and FCP 2288 ms.
findings.fix: Inject pdf.js only when a resume PDF is actually opened (create the script element on demand) instead of on every profile view. Find the load-time rAF that reads layout by searching profile.html for requestAnimationFrame callbacks that call getBoundingClientRect/offset*/scrollHeight, and move the read before any writes.
findings.risk: Low. The resume preview must wait for the script to load on first open.

desktop_perf_cursor.not_verified:
- **GPU work was not measured.** Frame pacing is rAF cadence on the main thread; I recorded no compositor or GPU trace. So I have not ruled out the backdrop-filter blur costing GPU time without showing up in the frame counts.
- **Scroll was simulated.** It sets scrollTop in rAF on the main thread. It is not a compositor-threaded trackpad or wheel scroll.
- **Several scroll runs were thin:**
  - /network had only 180 px to scroll.
  - On profile.html only 136 of 4539 px moved, likely because the page scrolls smoothly on its own; I did not confirm that.
  - The /messages iframe had no scrollable area (short thread list), so there is no scroll data for it.
- **Real-mouse hovers inside the /messages iframe did not complete.** Tagging found only 1 target (button.t-new-btn) and the hover chain timed out. The two long frames (229 and 178 ms) in that window have no script or style attribution and are most likely the harness.
- **60 Hz numbers are simulated, not measured on a 60 Hz display.** The simulation matches the live 30 fps and 120 Hz runs.
- **The Energy Saver explanation for 30 fps is inferred.** It rests on:
  - 2% battery, discharging;
  - an exact 33.3 ms cadence with no long tasks;
  - 120 fps after the machine was plugged in.
  A blank-page control on battery was not possible: `about:` is blocked, and the file:// control ran after charging started. I did not read chrome://settings.
- **The first pass's "per-page" numbers for /messages, profile and /network are invalid and were discarded.** The goto commands failed ("not responding"), so those numbers are /campus measured again.
- **Two pieces of test tooling were excluded:** the gstack browser's own injected UI (`div#gstack-ctrl` background-position shimmer, and the `gstack-status-pill` `blur(8px)`) is left out of all counts.
- **No live onboarding data.** The onboarding page was not loaded; its cursor numbers come from its code (factor 0.18) plus the simulation.
- **Mouse-driven effects were not isolated:**
  - the LeftNav glow (framer-motion spring driving a radial-gradient background, LeftNav.tsx:173-201, 270);
  - the MouseSpotlight 3D tilt on backdrop-blurred event cards.
  I did not confirm whether any sampled hover target was inside a spotlight card.
- **Lower-end hardware was not tested.**
- **Cold load was measured once.** Only /campus, and while the machine was on battery; the 120 Hz runs used a warm cache.
- **The polling re-render cost was not measured directly.**
- **No code was changed.** The recommended TAU of 17 ms is a proposal backed by simulation.
